prompt: Power rises upwards and interest to the right. Put each treatment in its quarter.
hint: High power and high interest is the top right.

prompt: Where does Diego sit on the grid, and what does that call for?
hint: He will not decide, and he will check.

choices.text: High power, high interest: he decides together with Paulo
choices.why: Paulo decides; Diego checks.

choices.text: High power, low interest: brief him only on outcomes
choices.why: He cares a great deal and decides little.

choices.text: Low power, high interest: keep informed
choices.why: Tell him what is happening and why.

choices.text: Low power, low interest: monitor
choices.why: He is very interested.

prompt: Why redraw the stakeholder map at each stage, by the lesson?

choices.text: Because people change jobs inside the company every few months
choices.why: The lesson's reason is the work, not turnover.

choices.text: Because the board asks for an updated map at every quarterly meeting
choices.why: No such request.

choices.text: Because the first map is always wrong and should be discarded
choices.why: It was right for its stage.

choices.text: Positions move as the work goes on
choices.why: Renata's interest rose with the money; Ligeiro rose when the pilot needed it.

prompt: Why did Marina's first delivery disappoint Paulo, by the lesson?

choices.text: Nobody agreed what the answer was for, by when, or what done looked like
choices.why: He imagined a ten-minute update; she built thirty-eight slides.

choices.text: The data was wrong
choices.why: The numbers held.

choices.text: She was late
choices.why: Not the problem described.

choices.text: Paulo forgot he asked
choices.why: No.

prompt: Which fields belong in the brief written back to the requester? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: The decision it informs

choices.text: Done when

choices.text: Out of scope

choices.text: The SQL the analyst will use
choices.why: Method is the analyst's, not part of the agreement.

prompt: Halfway through, the work makes Sandra a stakeholder nobody named. What is the rule?

choices.text: Absorb the change and mention it at the delivery
choices.why: That lets the delivery surprise the requester.

choices.text: Update the brief and tell the requester that week
choices.why: Analysis finds things; agreements are renegotiated in the open.

choices.text: Start a new project
choices.why: Not needed.

choices.text: Leave Sandra out
choices.why: She is now top right.

prompt: Two valuable, expensive requests collide. Who should decide which comes first?

choices.text: The analyst, because she knows the work and its effort better than anybody
choices.why: She shows the trade-off; she does not settle it between departments.

choices.text: Whoever asked first, since the request log records the order of arrival
choices.why: Order of arrival is not value.

choices.text: The person who sets priorities across teams
choices.why: Usually the analyst's manager.

choices.text: The louder department
choices.why: That is the problem being avoided.

prompt: Which of these is a "not now" the lesson recommends?

choices.text: I'm too busy for that this quarter, try asking somebody else
choices.why: A refusal with nothing attached.

choices.text: Send me an email with every detail and I will look at it eventually
choices.why: No date, no smaller version.

choices.text: That is not part of my job description at this company
choices.why: Not a delay; a wall.

choices.text: The overall rate now, the breakdown next month
choices.why: A smaller version first is easier to hear than no.

prompt: Why keep a request log visible to whoever sets your priorities?

choices.text: It shows exactly what would move to make room for a new request
choices.why: The strongest argument an analyst has.

choices.text: To prove you are busy
choices.why: It shows trade-offs, not effort.

choices.text: For performance reviews
choices.why: Not the reason.

choices.text: Because tools require it
choices.why: No.

prompt: Which line of the weekly update does the most work, by the lesson?

choices.text: Done this week
choices.why: Useful, and not the one.

choices.text: Early findings, marked as early
choices.why: People get used to them before they are final, and can correct them cheaply.

choices.text: Next week
choices.why: Useful, and not the one.

choices.text: A long list of the blockers that other teams have caused
choices.why: Not one of the four parts, and it would read as blame.

prompt: Put Marina's pre-meeting conversations in the order she held them.
hint: The person the finding is about comes first.

prompt: The Japanese name for preparing consensus in small conversations before the meeting is ___.

choices.why: The lesson says it is not manipulation at all.

choices.text: It depends on the board

prompt: How many minutes did Marina's second meeting take to approve the pilot?
hint: It confirmed a decision already prepared.

prompt: How often should the top-right stakeholders hear from you, by the lesson?

choices.text: Only at the final presentation, so that they see the finished work

choices.text: Every day, in a meeting that the whole team attends

choices.text: Whenever they ask for an update on the analysis
choices.why: Waiting to be asked is already late.

choices.text: Weekly
choices.why: Milestones for the top left; a note for the bottom right.

prompt: Sandra still disputes the finding after every conversation. What does the lesson say to do?

choices.text: Drop the finding to keep the relationship
choices.why: The finding is sound; the relationship survives a warning.

choices.text: Present it without telling her, so the room can judge it fresh

prompt: The marketing director owns the cancellation rate and was not in the first meeting. Where on the grid, and what next?

choices.text: Bottom left: monitor her occasionally and copy her on the final email
choices.why: She has power and a direct interest.

choices.text: Bottom right: keep her informed through the weekly update only
choices.why: She has more power than that.

choices.text: Nowhere: cancellations are an operations matter now that the cause is known
choices.why: The effect is still hers.

choices.text: Top right: see her alone, soon
choices.why: Nobody important should learn about your work in a meeting.
